html:
SMTO-RST-0021 — SMTO couldn't finish this backup export or import

GUID: 0edd01a2-d00e-5e7b-b52f-2f76ea30d680
Slug: backup-operation-unavailable
Domain: RST · Subsystem: backup

What happened

  • A safety check stopped this backup step, for example because the file is incomplete, from an unsupported version, too large, or the disk is low on space. SMTO only replaces your data after an import passes every check.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Data and read the message under Export / Import. It names the problem, such as a changed file, an unsupported version, or the 512 MiB limit. Each backup check has its own fix, and the message tells you which check failed.
  2. If the file may be incomplete or was edited, export a new backup with Export JSON on the SMTO that made it, then choose that new file. SMTO rejects any backup whose contents don't match the check it recorded when the file was made.
  3. Free up disk space on the computer running SMTO, then choose the backup file again under Import JSON to get a fresh preview. SMTO needs room for a test copy and a recovery copy of your data before it can accept an import.
  4. If the message says an import is already pending, select Cancel pending import, or restart SMTO to apply it, before importing another file. Only one import can wait for a restart at a time.

What success looks like

  • The preview lists your conversations, tasks and other items, and Import on next restart becomes available once you tick the confirmation box; or your exported file downloads.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the backup file's name and size, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit the backup file by hand, and don't delete the recovery copy SMTO keeps on this computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Settings backup export, preview, staging or startup import was rejected by data_transfer validation (request origin, content type or 512 MiB size limit, unsupported format version, checksum mismatch, invalid stores or references, insufficient free space, or a conflicting pending or in-progress import).

What this means

  • Backup/import validation rejects request authority/format/bounds, inconsistent schemas/digests/paths, incomplete ownership snapshots, insufficient space or conflicting pending/recovery state. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Backup/import validation rejects request authority/format/bounds, inconsistent schemas/digests/paths, incomplete ownership snapshots, insufficient space or conflicting pending/recovery state.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the exact preview/import stage and validation condition; this aggregate category does not identify one universal storage repair.

How to fix it

  • Read the BackupError detail returned by the /api/agent/settings/data routes (shown in the Export / Import panel). Re-export to fix checksum or format mismatches, keep uploads under 512 MiB as application/json from the same origin, free space in the state directory, and cancel or apply an existing pending import before staging another; if a startup import reports changed storage paths, restore the original storage configuration first.
  • Read the reported backup condition. Check format compatibility, complete contents, available disk space and pending imports. Preserve the existing data and preview the backup again before confirming an import.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported fresh preview validates complete compatible contents and any deliberate import follows the current confirmed token.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
